owner_source.proposal: For genuinely difficult Work tasks, start with GPT-5.6 Sol at Extra High. If that attempt genuinely fails, try GPT-6 Astra at Extra High on the same bounded task to see whether it does better.
owner_source.confirmation: Owner agreed to try the strategy, keep task/model results in GitHub, and review the evidence after a few weeks.

normalized_outcome: During the trial window, ordinary residual execution continues to use the lowest sufficient Sol tier. Genuinely difficult residual execution starts with GPT-5.6 Sol Extra High. A GPT-6 Astra Extra High attempt is admitted as a matched challenger only after Chat classifies the Sol failure and verifies that the failure is not primarily a bad plan, missing access/context, or a mechanical/transient problem. Preserve task/base/directive/permissions/direct endpoint as closely as practical so the comparison is informative. Track privacy-safe task category, exact model/effort, endpoint result, scope/gate violations, retries/interventions, observable allowance use, failure classification, and challenger outcome in GitHub. Review the accumulated evidence after approximately three weeks; do not mutate routing policy automatically from telemetry.
preserved_requirements: Chat reasons first and delegates only the bounded residual execution task.
Simple and ordinary work must not be run at expensive reasoning levels without a concrete need.

Work still performs the existing too-low/too-high reasoning-level sanity check; the active difficult-task calibration baseline is an owner-authorized reason that Sol XHigh is not considered wasteful merely because a lower tier might sometimes succeed.
A model switch does not repair CHAT_PLAN_DEFECT, ACCESS_CONTEXT_DEFECT, or a clearly mechanical/transient failure.
No paid credits or additional spend are authorized by this requirement.
